application_status.label: Programme active; annual issuance limit applies
application_status.detail: The Italy–Japan Working Holiday programme began on 1 April 2026. Official guidance says there is an annual issuance limit and applications cannot be accepted once it has been reached; check the responsible mission before relying on late-year availability.

change_control.review_note: Italy ruleset verified against the current Embassy of Japan in Italy and Consulate-General of Japan in Milan Working Holiday guidance.

summary_facts.label: Residence
summary_facts.value: Italian citizen resident in Italy at application

summary_facts.label: Funds baseline
summary_facts.value: €1,800 initial living funds plus return ticket, or about €3,800 without a return ticket

eligibility_rules.label: Are you an Italian citizen?
eligibility_rules.fail_message: This Working Holiday route is for Italian citizens.

eligibility_rules.label: Are you resident in Italy at the time of application?
eligibility_rules.fail_message: Italian Working Holiday applicants must reside in Italy when applying.

eligibility_rules.label: Your age at the time you expect to apply
eligibility_rules.fail_message: The Italian Working Holiday age range is 18–30 inclusive at application.

eligibility_rules.label: Is your primary purpose to holiday in Japan?
eligibility_rules.fail_message: The main purpose must be a holiday; part-time work is incidental to financing the trip.

eligibility_rules.label: Will dependants without their own eligible status accompany you?
eligibility_rules.fail_message: Dependants cannot accompany the principal applicant unless they independently hold an appropriate status.

eligibility_rules.label: Can you truthfully meet the health, insurance and no-criminal-record requirements?
eligibility_rules.fail_message: The Italian programme requires adequate health coverage, good health and no criminal record.

funds_rule.input_label: Funds shown in your Italian bank statements (€)
funds_rule.no_ticket_note: Without a return ticket, official guidance requires about €2,000 sufficient to cover one plus at least €1,800 for initial living costs.

jurisdiction.label: Japanese mission responsible for your Italian residence
jurisdiction.description: Italian residents apply through Rome or Milan according to consular jurisdiction. The procedures differ: Rome pre-screens documents by email and confirms an appointment; Milan currently accepts complete printed applications without an appointment.
jurisdiction.ui_help: Choose the Japanese mission responsible for the region where you live.

options.label: Emilia-Romagna, Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Liguria, Lombardia, Piemonte, Trentino-Alto Adige, Valle d'Aosta or Veneto
options.mission_detail: Milan handles these eight northern regions. Current Working Holiday guidance says no appointment is required; bring the complete printed application.

options.label: Elsewhere in Italy
options.mission_label: Embassy of Japan in Italy — Rome
options.mission_detail: The Embassy Working Holiday procedure instructs applicants to email the required documents first, wait for a response, then attend a confirmed appointment in Rome.

options.label: I am not resident in Italy
options.mission_label: Italian Working Holiday route may not apply
options.mission_detail: The current Working Holiday rules require Italian citizenship and residence in Italy at the time of application.
options.issue: The Italy Working Holiday route requires the applicant to be an Italian citizen resident in Italy at the time of application.

document_checklist.title: Valid Italian passport
document_checklist.description: Passport needs at least two blank pages and validity extending at least three months beyond the planned stay.

document_checklist.title: Visa application form
document_checklist.description: Complete the current official visa application form.

document_checklist.title: Recent photograph
document_checklist.description: Provide a photograph taken within the previous six months and attach it as instructed.

document_checklist.title: Curriculum Vitae
document_checklist.description: Prepare the current Working Holiday CV form.

document_checklist.title: Outline of planned activities
document_checklist.description: Complete the official outline of activities planned for the Working Holiday stay.

document_checklist.title: Statement of intent
document_checklist.description: Prepare the free-format statement explaining why you are applying for the Working Holiday visa.

document_checklist.title: Three months of bank statements
document_checklist.description: Provide bank statements in the applicant's name for the previous three months and meet the applicable ticket/funds baseline.

document_checklist.title: Return-flight booking if already reserved
document_checklist.description: Provide the return-flight reservation if already booked; otherwise ensure sufficient additional funds for the return ticket.

document_checklist.title: National Health Insurance pledge or adequate coverage
document_checklist.description: Provide the required National Health Insurance pledge or qualifying health-insurance evidence under the current instructions.

document_checklist.title: Personal-data consent form
document_checklist.description: Provide the required consent form for use of personal data.

preparation_checklist.title: Check annual-cap availability
preparation_checklist.description: The programme has an annual issuance limit; confirm availability with the mission responsible for your residence.

preparation_checklist.title: Confirm Rome vs Milan jurisdiction
preparation_checklist.description: Milan covers the eight northern regions listed in the planner; other Italian residents should follow the Embassy in Rome procedure.

preparation_checklist.title: Follow your mission's submission method
preparation_checklist.description: Rome uses email pre-screening plus a confirmed appointment; Milan currently accepts complete printed applications without an appointment.

preparation_checklist.title: Plan for the three-month visa validity window
preparation_checklist.description: Current guidance says entry into Japan must occur within three months after the Working Holiday visa is issued.

preparation_checklist.title: Run a final official-source check
preparation_checklist.description: Re-check annual-cap status, documents and local submission instructions immediately before applying.
